sketchMechanisms: The Maybe type and pattern matching on Nothing — a value that is both a valid computational result and an existential statement
The 'never' type represents values that can never occur — a function returning 'never' is one that never finishes or always throws, and no value inhabits the type
Prolog's closed-world assumption: anything not provable from the knowledge base is considered false — what is unspoken is untrue
